summary: The Work Explorer's session rows stopped being labels you cannot click. Activating one now opens the set's own spec.md positioned at that session's `### Session N of M:` block — revealed at the top of the editor with an empty cursor on the heading, so the surrounding context and the configuration block stay a scroll away. It goes through the EXISTING `dabblerSessionSets.openSpec` rather than a parallel command: `openSpec` reads a session number off its argument, so there is still one answer to "which file is the spec" and one message when it is missing, and a set row through the same command still opens at the top exactly as before. The one new rule — which lines belong to session N — lives in a pure module (`providers/specSectionLocator.ts`) that borrows `sessionStepModel.scanSessionHeads` instead of carrying a second heading regex, so the step parser and the reveal cannot disagree about where a session begins; a heading inside a fenced sample is not a section, which is the falsifier that keeps a spec from opening at its own documentation template. Everything unanswerable degrades to the real file at the top: no session number, an unreadable spec, a ledger ahead of its spec, a malformed heading, or a throw inside the reveal. The spec read happens on the CLICK, never on the tree scan, so the measured no-extra-read constraint is untouched. Verification: both discovery lenses returned VERIFIED with zero Critical/Major findings; one nit recorded and deliberately not fixed (an already-open spec.md keeps its scroll position on the degradation path, matching the set row's long-standing behaviour).

reason.specifics: Session 3 hangs a context menu on the very node this session made clickable and reuses the same openSpec plumbing for its artifact QuickPick. The live context that matters is this session's: the contextValue vocabulary, the menu-parity test's forward and backward assertions, and why session-row menu entries are deliberately absent rather than forgotten. No blocker, no cost pressure, no capability gap; verification stays cross-provider regardless.
